people.name: Elon Musk
people.history: Co-founded Zip2 and X.com (later PayPal), then built Tesla and SpaceX. Bought Twitter in 2022 (now X) and founded xAI.

ecology.reason: Tesla makes cars, a material footprint under the rubric; rockets and xAI data centres add energy use. xAI is sued under the Clean Air Act, accused of installing gas turbines without permits at a Mississippi data-centre plant in 2025; a judge refused to dismiss the case, which is pending. Emissions avoided by Tesla’s electric cars are not independently assessed here.

politics.reason: Largest US political donor of 2024 (more than $290 million) and of the 2025–26 midterm cycle ($445.5 million in outside spending, per OpenSecrets). Led the DOGE cost-cutting effort in 2025, which targeted agencies holding contracts with his companies; those companies received at least $38 billion in public contracts, loans, subsidies and tax credits. Settlements of two voter suits against him and America PAC over the 2024 $1 million giveaway await court approval; no liability was found.

social.reason: Company-level problems are documented: a jury found Tesla partly responsible for a fatal Autopilot crash (2025, upheld 2026); California is trying a race-discrimination case over Tesla’s Fremont plant, which Tesla denies; the EU fined X €120 million in 2025 under the Digital Services Act and is investigating sexualised Grok images on X. None is a personal finding.

legal.reason: Personal civil liability: a San Francisco jury found him liable in March 2026 for misleading Twitter shareholders; the judge later set aside one of the two statements and the judgment is on appeal. Charged by the SEC with securities fraud in 2018 over Tesla tweets, he paid a $20 million personal penalty without admitting or denying the charges; settled a second SEC case in 2026 ($1.5 million), on the same terms. Won a 2023 investor trial and, in 2025, the appeal restoring his Tesla pay package.

unresolved.reason: Named defendant in pending matters: his appeal of the Twitter shareholder judgment, and the giveaway settlements awaiting court approval. The January 2026 Epstein files include 2012–2013 emails in which he discussed visiting Epstein’s island, at odds with his earlier statement that he declined invitations. He says some emails could be misinterpreted. No authority has accused him of a crime. A congressman says about half of the six million identified pages were not released.

people.counterweights: Tesla accelerated the shift to electric cars; SpaceX lowered launch costs.

people.name: Larry Page
people.history: Co-founded Google in 1998 with Sergey Brin.

ecology.reason: Data centres and electronics supply chains: an indirect footprint. Google reports that its electricity use rose 37% in 2025, its largest increase, and that supply-chain emissions, about 80% of its total, rose 25% while operational emissions fell 2%. It reports matching all its electricity use with renewable purchases and says its climate goals are getting harder to reach.

politics.reason: Page holds 27.4% of Alphabet's voting power and Sergey Brin 25.3%, together a majority of votes in YouTube's parent. In 2025 YouTube and Alphabet agreed to pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump's suit over his account suspension, $22 million of it to the trust funding the White House ballroom; CBS reported that Google also gave to the ballroom, amount not stated. Alphabet's federal lobbying was $4.13 million in early 2026. This research found no personal political donations by Page.

social.reason: US courts found that Google illegally maintained monopolies in search (2024) and online advertising technology (2025), both under appeal, and a jury found its Android app store an illegal monopoly, upheld on appeal in 2025. EU courts upheld fines for favouring its own services. Google agreed in 2025 to pay Texas $1.375 billion over alleged tracking of location and biometric data. These are company acts.

legal.reason: Company-level court findings: US monopoly rulings in search, ad tech and app distribution; EU fines of €2.4 billion (Shopping) and €4.1 billion (Android) upheld as final; a €2.95 billion EU ad tech fine under appeal; a €1.49 billion AdSense fine annulled in 2024. Settlements of $1.375 billion (Texas) and $700 million (Play Store). Page was named in shareholder suits settled in 2020 and 2025 with reforms paid by Alphabet; no personal penalty or finding.

unresolved.reason: Pending at company level: Google's appeal and the DOJ's cross-appeal in the search case, Google's announced appeals in the US ad tech case and against the €2.95 billion EU ad tech fine, and the Commission's appeal over AdSense. In May 2023 the US Virgin Islands asked a court to let it serve Page through Alphabet with a subpoena for documents in its Epstein-related suit against JPMorgan; the report alleged no wrongdoing by him. No pending case names him.

people.counterweights: Page's family foundation, the Carl Victor Page Memorial Foundation, reported 2024 grants including $235 million to a donor-advised fund, whose onward grants are not public, $10 million to Climate Breakthrough and $6 million to Windward Fund.

people.name: Sergey Brin
people.history: Co-founded Google in 1998 with Larry Page.

ecology.reason: Technology and platforms: data-centre electricity and electronics supply chains. Google reports that its electricity use rose 37% in 2025, its largest increase, and that supply-chain emissions, about 80% of its total, rose 25% while scope 1 and 2 emissions fell 2%. It reports matching all its electricity use with renewable purchases.

politics.reason: By mid-August 2026 had given $102 million that year to a committee backing ballot measures that could block California's proposed billionaire tax, per state data reported by the Los Angeles Times; AP put his share of its $333 million at about 30%. Holds 25.3% of Alphabet's voting power. YouTube directed $22 million of a 2025 Trump settlement to the White House ballroom trust. No documented political favour.

social.reason: US courts found that Google illegally maintained monopolies in search (2024), now under appeal, and online advertising (2025), which Google plans to appeal, and a jury found against its Play Store in Epic's case, upheld on appeal in 2025. EU courts confirmed fines over Shopping (2024) and Android (2026). Google agreed in 2025 to pay Texas $1.375 billion over alleged tracking. These are company acts.

legal.reason: Company-level court findings: US monopoly rulings in search and ad tech, the Epic verdict, and EU fines of €2.4 billion (Shopping) and €4.1 billion (Android) now final. Brin was named in shareholder suits settled in 2020 and 2025 with reforms paid by Alphabet, and personally sued in 2024 over his plane's 2023 crash, one suit settled in 2025 on unreported terms. No personal penalty or finding against him.

unresolved.reason: Epstein files released in January 2026 show Brin visited Epstein's island, on an undated occasion, and corresponded with Ghislaine Maxwell in 2003; he did not respond to the New York Times. A widow's 2024 wrongful-death suit against him was last reported pending in September 2024. At company level, the US search appeals, a planned ad tech appeal, EU ad tech and DMA fines and a $2.1 billion damages award are pending.

people.counterweights: Forbes reported in 2025 that Brin had spent about $1.75 billion on Parkinson's research and made nearly $900 million in grants in 2024, out of $3.9 billion in lifetime giving; over $1 billion in stock went to a 501(c)(4) whose spending is not stated.

people.name: Jeff Bezos
people.history: Founded Amazon in 1994. Also owns Blue Origin and The Washington Post.

ecology.reason: Mass retail, logistics and data centres. Amazon's own figures show absolute emissions up 16% in 2025, with Scope 3 up 20% and Scope 2 electricity up 34%, which Amazon attributes to data-centre use and electrification; its net-zero target is 2040.

politics.reason: Owns The Washington Post, and in 2025 personally set its opinion section to defend personal liberties and free markets. Amazon's lobbying not assessed here.

social.reason: Amazon paid $2.5 billion in 2025 to settle FTC charges that it enrolled customers in Prime without clear consent and made cancelling hard, without admitting wrongdoing. In 2026 it agreed to settle a class action alleging unpaid return refunds (preliminarily approved), and in 2024 it settled OSHA ergonomics cases from warehouse inspections.

legal.reason: Company settlement above $1 billion (FTC Prime case, 2025); no personal case. Italy's 2021 abuse-of-dominance fine was cut to €752.4 million in 2026, and Amazon said it would appeal. Luxembourg's €746 million GDPR fine was annulled in 2026 on procedure, with the main breaches confirmed. The European Commission lost its state-aid case against Amazon in 2023.

unresolved.reason: The FTC's antitrust case against Amazon, joined by states, is due for trial on 29 March 2027. The FTC and 22 states also sued in August 2026 over alleged hidden ad-auction surcharges, and California's price case is set for trial in 2027. All are company-level; none names Bezos as a defendant.

people.counterweights: The Bezos Day 1 Families Fund has donated more than $850 million in homelessness grants since 2018. Fortune reports the Bezos Earth Fund had deployed about $2.4 billion of a $10 billion climate pledge by 2026, without saying how much was paid out.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.history: Co-founded Facebook in 2004; controls Meta through voting shares.

ecology.reason: Indirect footprint through data centres. Louisiana regulators approved three gas plants in 2025, about 2.3 gigawatts, to power Meta's largest data centre; Meta says it will match the site's use with clean energy. No major environmental incident found.

politics.reason: Controls platforms central to political communication worldwide. Meta put $65 million into super PACs for 2026 state races and paid $25 million in 2025 to settle Donald Trump's suit over his account suspension, $22 million of it for his future library. Zuckerberg was named in 2026 to a presidential science and technology council, which is advisory only.

social.reason: Meta agreed in 2026 to pay up to about $18.6 billion to 52 attorneys general over teen mental health, about $5.3 billion of it conditional on rivals; no admission was reported. Juries in Los Angeles and New Mexico found it liable for harm to young users in 2026; Meta is challenging both. Facebook paid $5 billion in 2019 to settle FTC privacy charges. In November 2025 a judge rejected the FTC's case that Meta holds a monopoly today; the FTC has appealed.

legal.reason: Company outcomes above $1 billion: the $5 billion FTC penalty (2019), a $1.4 billion Texas biometric settlement (2024), the 2026 youth settlement and a $25 billion New Mexico penalty (2026) Meta will appeal; EU fines include €1.2 billion and €798 million. Zuckerberg settled a shareholder suit for $190 million paid by insurers, without admission. No personal criminal case or penalty.

unresolved.reason: Zuckerberg is a named defendant in a District of Columbia suit seeking to hold him personally liable over Cambridge Analytica-era privacy failures; a judge refused to dismiss it in April 2026. These are allegations. At company level the FTC is appealing its monopoly loss, Meta is challenging the New Mexico judgments and the Los Angeles verdict, and securities class actions continue.

people.counterweights: The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Foundation, with Zuckerberg as trustee, disbursed about $389 million in 2024 and $216 million in 2023, per its IRS filings.

people.name: Larry Ellison
people.history: Co-founded Oracle in 1977.

ecology.reason: Technology and platforms: data-centre electricity and electronics supply chains.

politics.reason: Major Republican donor: about $35 million in 2020–2022 to a super PAC backing Senator Tim Scott, as reported by Business Insider. Set to hold a minority voting interest of about 35.5% in the merged Paramount Skydance, and personally guaranteed $40.4 billion of equity for its bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, owner of CNN. His foundation has donated or pledged at least £257m to the Tony Blair Institute, amount paid not stated; no illegality is alleged.

social.reason: Oracle agreed in 2024 to pay $115 million to settle a class action alleging it collected and sold people's data without consent; it denies wrongdoing. Other labour and market-power concerns are not sourced here.

legal.reason: Oracle paid more than $23 million in 2022 to resolve SEC charges that subsidiaries bribed foreign officials, its second FCPA resolution. In 2005 Ellison agreed to give $100 million to charity in Oracle's name and pay $22 million in fees to settle a shareholder suit alleging insider trading; no admission was reported. Delaware courts ruled for him in 2023 and 2025 in a suit over Oracle's NetSuite purchase.

unresolved.reason: Investor class actions filed in early 2026 allege Oracle misled investors about its AI data-centre spending and borrowing; Ellison is named in the bondholder suit. These are allegations and no ruling on them was found.

people.counterweights: The Larry Ellison Foundation disbursed about $76 million in 2024 and $55 million in 2023, per its IRS filings.

legal_record.nature: Investor class actions (Oracle; Ellison named in one)
legal_record.summary: In January and February 2026 investors filed two proposed class actions over Oracle's AI data-centre spending: a bondholder suit in New York state court naming Ellison among the defendants, alleging offering documents hid planned borrowing, and a securities suit in Delaware federal court. These are allegations; no liability has been found.

legal_record.nature: Derivative suit over the NetSuite purchase
legal_record.summary: Oracle shareholders alleged in a derivative suit that Ellison, a co-founder and large holder in both companies, forced Oracle to overpay for NetSuite in 2016. After trial the Court of Chancery ruled for the defendants in 2023, finding the special committee's negotiation untainted by his influence, and the Delaware Supreme Court affirmed in January 2025.

In 2024 Oracle agreed to pay $115 million to settle a federal class action (Katz-Lacabe v. Oracle America) alleging it captured, compiled and sold people's online and offline data without consent. Oracle denies the allegations and any wrongdoing, and agreed to stop capturing certain user data.

legal_record.outcome: Resolved 2022: over $23m, neither admitted nor denied
legal_record.summary: In September 2022 the SEC found that Oracle subsidiaries in Turkey, the UAE and India used off-book slush funds in 2016 to 2019 to bribe foreign officials, and Oracle paid over $23 million without admitting or denying the findings. It was Oracle's second FCPA resolution, after a 2012 case over Oracle India.

legal_record.outcome: Settled 2005: $100m to charity, $22m in fees, no admission
legal_record.summary: In November 2005, more than ten years ago, a San Mateo County court approved Ellison's settlement of a shareholder derivative suit alleging insider trading in his sale of about $900 million of Oracle stock in January 2001. He agreed to give $100 million to charity in Oracle's name and pay $22 million in legal fees; the report records no admission of wrongdoing.

people.name: Bernard Arnault & family
people.history: Took over his family’s construction firm, then built LVMH from 1984 into the largest luxury group.

ecology.reason: Luxury goods: leather, textiles, metals and global retail.

politics.reason: LVMH owns the national dailies Le Parisien and Les Échos and in 2024 took over the weekly Paris Match. In 2022 Arnault corrected by letter, the same day, a statement he made to a Senate inquiry into media concentration about LVMH's offer for Paris Match. Personal political donations and LVMH's lobbying were not assessed here.

social.reason: In 2024 a Milan court placed a Dior manufacturing unit under administration over labour exploitation at subcontractors; one bag cost €53 to supply and sold for €2,600. In 2025 the Italian competition authority closed its probe with Dior committing €2 million to victims, without a finding against Dior. In 2025 the same court found Loro Piana had negligently facilitated exploitation at subcontractors. Both administrations were lifted early.

legal.reason: Court-imposed administration of two subsidiaries, Manufactures Dior (2024) and Loro Piana (2025); neither was under criminal investigation. In 2021 LVMH agreed to a €10 million fine under a prosecutor agreement over possible influence peddling, without a declaration of guilt; an ex-spy chief who consulted for LVMH was convicted in 2025 and said he would appeal. In 2013 the AMF fined LVMH €8 million over its Hermès stake-building. Arnault has not been personally charged in these matters.

unresolved.reason: Bernard Arnault and LVMH are named defendants in a pending Paris civil suit by Hermès heir Nicolas Puech, who claims about €14 billion over shares he says were diverted to LVMH; LVMH and its shareholder deny it. A related criminal investigation has placed Swiss lawyers under formal investigation; no charge against LVMH or Arnault is reported. A privacy suit by François Ruffin against LVMH is pending, and Givenchy Italia and Bulgari have been drawn into a Milan labour probe without charges.

people.counterweights: The Arnault family gave €10 million to the food charity Restos du Cœur in 2023. LVMH reports halving Scope 1 and 2 emissions from energy against 2019 by 2025; Scope 3, 96% of its footprint, fell 13% from 2023 (company figures).

people.name: Jensen Huang
people.history: Co-founded Nvidia in 1993.

ecology.reason: Nvidia designs chips and outsources their manufacture, so its footprint is indirect. It reports matching all its electricity use with clean power, partly through certificates. Its reported Scope 3 emissions, mostly from suppliers, rose by about half in a year to 10.7 million tonnes, partly under a revised method. The electricity demand of the AI data centres its chips power is not settled by these figures.

politics.reason: Nvidia gave $25 million to the White House ballroom fund, tied for the largest gift on an internal donor list obtained by the Washington Post, and Huang said in 2025 that he had donated, without a disclosed amount. In 2025 Nvidia and AMD were reported to have agreed to pay the US government 15% of certain China chip revenue for export licences; the President said Huang negotiated the rate down. No finding of an improper favour has been made.

social.reason: Nvidia's market power is under regulatory scrutiny. China's regulator issued a preliminary finding in 2025 that Nvidia breached its anti-monopoly law and the conditions of the Mellanox approval, and Reuters reports that the US Justice Department is examining its deals and sales practices. Neither has reached a final decision. Labour and supply-chain conditions were not checked.

legal.reason: In 2022 Nvidia paid a $5.5 million SEC penalty over undisclosed cryptomining revenue, without admitting or denying the findings. No individual was charged. No court finding against the company or Huang was found.

unresolved.reason: Huang is a named defendant in a certified shareholder class action alleging that he and Nvidia misled investors about crypto-mining revenue in 2017-2018, and in related derivative suits; these are allegations not yet tried. At company level, China's antitrust investigation is open and a US Justice Department inquiry is reported.

people.counterweights: The Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation gave $50 million to Oregon State University in 2022, but in 2023 most of its payouts went to a donor-advised fund, which need not disclose its grants. Nvidia reports matching all its electricity use with clean power in fiscal 2025 and 2026.

legal_record.summary: Reuters reported in October 2026, citing two people familiar with the matter, that the Justice Department is questioning Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion Hugging Face purchase within a wider review, begun under Biden, of its deals and sales practices, including whether it offered bigger chip allocations to buyers of its other products. No enforcement action has been reported.

Nvidia's mid-2026 quarterly filing lists derivative suits over the same alleged misstatements, three of them captioned against Huang, filed in 2019 in federal court in Delaware and in 2023 in the Delaware Court of Chancery. They seek damages or disgorgement of stock-sale profits and governance reforms, and are stayed until the securities class action is resolved.

A shareholder class action alleges that Nvidia and Huang misled investors in 2017-2018 about how much revenue came from crypto mining. Revived by the Ninth Circuit in 2023, it survived a Supreme Court appeal dismissed in December 2024 and a class was certified in March 2026; these are allegations and liability has not been decided.

In September 2025 China's market regulator SAMR said a preliminary investigation found Nvidia had violated the Anti-Monopoly Law and the conditions of its 2020 approval of the Mellanox takeover, without specifying the conduct. It moved to a further investigation before any penalty; no final decision was found.

In May 2022 the SEC found that Nvidia's quarterly filings for fiscal 2018 reported gaming revenue growth without disclosing that cryptomining drove a significant part of it. Nvidia paid a $5.5 million penalty without admitting or denying the findings; no individual was charged.

people.name: Warren Buffett
people.history: Built Berkshire Hathaway from a textile company into a conglomerate from 1965.

ecology.reason: Berkshire’s utilities own about 6,900 MW of coal capacity and BNSF had about $3 billion in coal freight revenue in 2025. US Forest Service reports found power lines of PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, caused or probably caused two 2020 wildfires; PacifiCorp agreed to pay $575 million to settle federal claims over six fires and denies liability. Berkshire reports a 30% cut in its energy unit’s emissions since 2005.

politics.reason: Not checked individually. Default for a large company.

social.reason: Company-level problems are documented at Berkshire subsidiaries: a 2023 federal jury found HomeServices of America took part in a conspiracy that had the purpose or effect of inflating home sellers’ commissions, and a federal judge found BNSF knowingly ran oil trains across Swinomish land beyond its easement. Both later settled. No finding against him personally.

legal.reason: Company outcomes at Berkshire and its subsidiaries; no personal record found. Court findings against BNSF (trespass, nearly $400 million, settled 2025) and HomeServices (commission conspiracy, $1.8 billion jointly, settled for $250 million). PacifiCorp agreed to pay $575 million to the US over wildfires, denying liability. OFAC fined Berkshire $4.1 million in 2020 over a subsidiary’s Iran sales.

unresolved.reason: Pending at company level: the Oregon Supreme Court heard argument in November 2026 on a 2023 jury verdict against PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, over four 2020 wildfires. The Court of Appeals reversed the verdict earlier in 2026, and about 2,000 further claims may depend on the outcome. Nothing personal found.

people.counterweights: Has given five foundations, including the Gates Foundation, Berkshire shares worth roughly $60 billion when given since 2006, per AP; his 2026 gift went to four family foundations only. Berkshire reports a 30% emissions cut at its energy unit since 2005.

legal_record.outcome: Jury verdict 2023, reversed on appeal 2026; before the Oregon Supreme Court
legal_record.entity: PacifiCorp (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, which Berkshire Hathaway wholly owns)
legal_record.summary: In 2023 an Oregon jury found PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, grossly negligent, reckless and willful over four 2020 fires; awards so far exceed $1 billion to about 200 survivors. The Court of Appeals reversed the verdict earlier in 2026, and the Oregon Supreme Court heard argument on 3 November 2026; about 2,000 further claims may depend on it.

legal_record.nature: US claims over fires started by power lines (PacifiCorp)
legal_record.entity: PacifiCorp (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, which Berkshire Hathaway wholly owns)
legal_record.summary: US Forest Service reports found that power lines of PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, caused the 2020 Slater fire and were the probable cause of the Archie Creek fire. In February 2026 PacifiCorp agreed to pay $575 million to settle US claims that its lines negligently started six 2020 and 2022 fires on public land; it denies liability.

legal_record.nature: Trespass suit by the Swinomish tribe (BNSF)
legal_record.outcome: Judge found trespass 2023; settled 2025 on confidential terms
